A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WIRE research and contain 18 readable pages, including Figures 1–4, Tables 1–12 and Appendices A.1–A.7. Text, equations and visual material support a reliable comparison without material gaps.

before.justification: v4 reports original synthetic graph experiments, point-cloud classification and segmentation, graph benchmark evaluations and ablations in Section 4 and Appendix A.

after.justification: v5 retains these original experimental outcomes, including WIRE results in Tables 1–4 and 8–12 and the attention analysis in Figure 4.

M1.justification: The spectral-feature construction and query/key rotation procedure remain unchanged. Algorithm 1 explicitly adds eigenvalue-weighted coordinates, but that construction already appeared in v4's Theorem 3; this clarifies an existing variant.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same monochromatic-subgraph and shortest-path tasks, ModelNet40 and ShapeNet point clouds, and graph benchmarks. The appendix evaluations retain the same dataset and scenario coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain the same methods: no-WIRE controls, NoPE and Cartesian RoPE point-cloud baselines, and Performer, softmax, SGFormer and BigBird baselines. No comparator is added or removed within an experiment.

E3.justification: Section 4 and Appendix A retain the same splits, preprocessing, metrics, model configurations, feature-dimension sweeps and training budgets. The hyperparameters in Tables 6–7 are unchanged, and no new evaluation protocol appears.

E4.justification: The spectral-dimension ablations, WIRE-removal attention analysis in Figure 4, and alternative-attention and RWPE evaluations are retained unchanged. The new oversquashing discussion introduces an interpretation without additional experimental analysis.

E5.justification: The four-run synthetic standard errors, single-seed point-cloud reporting and dataset-dependent benchmark repetition counts in Appendices A.1, A.3 and A.4 are unchanged. Uncertainty reporting practices remain the same.

E6.justification: Empirical scores in Tables 1–4 and 8–12 match across versions. The training curves and attention-pattern panels in Figures 3–4 also match; no empirical result entries or findings are added, removed or corrected.

T1.justification: Theorem 3 replaces q_i^T k_j(1 − omega^2 R/2) + O(omega^4) with the exact expectation q_i^T k_j exp(−omega^2 R/2), replacing the Taylor argument with a Gaussian cosine expectation. v5 also corrects the Gaussian covariance to omega^2 I and the sine-term sign. Section 3.1 adds a Laplacian-pseudoinverse argument supporting expressivity with full weighted spectral features and explaining the loss of that guarantee under truncation.

C1.justification: The abstract removes the asymptotic restriction from the effective-resistance claim, reflecting the exact expectation result. The central claims about graph RoPE, recovery on grids, linear-attention compatibility and empirical benefits retain their scope.

C2.justification: Section 3.1 newly qualifies expressivity for truncated spectral features. Section 3.3 removes the approximation-error caveat while retaining the expectation-versus-single-instantiation limitation, updates the gauge-invariance interpretation, and adds a tentative connection between resistance-based attention modulation and GNN oversquashing.

D1.justification: Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware, training information and code-access disclosures are retained. Appendix A.4 corrects an equation reference from (13) to (2), but supplies no new implementation or reproducibility information.

R1.justification: v5 adds Black et al. (2023) and Di Giovanni et al. (2023) for the oversquashing connection, and Chen et al. (2024) on masked graph transformers. It removes Dasgupta and Gupta (2003) alongside the Johnson–Lindenstrauss footnote. Broader research positioning is retained.

P1.justification: Localized revisions expand Algorithm 1 and the theoretical explanations, replace 'direct product' with 'concatenation', repair appendix and equation references, and update contribution credits for Theorem 3. The overall section and appendix organization remains unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2 moves from page 4 to page 5, and Figure 3 from page 7 to page 8, with accompanying text and box reflow. The same four figures and twelve tables remain, without substantive plot or table redesign.

improvement.justification: v5 improves theoretical precision through the exact, consistently parameterized derivation in Theorem 3 and the explicit expressivity limitation for truncated features in Section 3.1. Corrected cross-references also improve clarity. These are focused gains in rigor and explanation: the empirical evidence remains intact, and the limitation concerning a single learned WIRE instantiation is preserved.
